page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Signature at the foot left, catchword at the foot right. Right margin holds only a red handwritten annotation, which is not printed and is noted below. Left margin holds a handwritten mark, also not printed.

main_text.p: tiplicem doctrinam Ecclesiæ[?] Christi ministrandi occasionem præriperent. Deinde quantavis eruditione & sanctitate cōspicui fuerint clarissimi Ecclesię Do-ctores, non tamen ullis seculis exhauri-re potuerunt largissimum eloquiorum Dei fontem. Quid fontem dico? Imo mare est scriptura divina, ut D. Ambrosius lib. 7. epist. ait, habens in se sensus profundos, altitudine propheticorum ænigmatum, in quod mare plurima introierunt flumina. Sunt ergo & fluuij[?] dulces atq; perspicui, sunt & fontes nivei, qui saliant in vitam æternam, sunt & sermones boni, sicut favi mellis, & gratæ sententiæ, quæ animos audientium spirituali quodam potu irrigent, & præceptorum moralium suavitate mulceant. Diversa igitur scripturarum divi-narum fluenta. Habes quod primum bi-bas, habes quod secundum, habes quod postremum. Collige aquam Christi, il-lam quæ laudat Dominum. Collige a-quam de pluribus locis, quam effundũt

page.notes: Red handwritten marginal note at right ("Ambrosius de S. Scriptura.") is later manuscript annotation, not printed, so omitted. Mark at left margin is handwriting, omitted. Faint show-through at the lower left is omitted. "Ecclesiæ" in the first line and "fluuij" at the end of the paragraph are doubtful: the ligature for the ending is hard to read, so both are marked [?]. The word-initial "tiplicem" appears cut off at the top of the line in the scan.
